name: Kodi
param_style: PrepareSQL printf-style (%i, %s, %u, %f, %02d) with values inlined and quoted by Kodi; normalised to ?N for per-call values, literals for column numbers, media types and enums
schema_source: CREATE statements quoted from xbmc/video/VideoDatabaseDDL.cpp and xbmc/music/MusicDatabase.cpp (GPL: only what the queries need); video and music DBs merged into one file, music genre(idGenre, strGenre) mapped onto the video genre table via generated-column aliases
data_scale: scale 1: 5000 movies (+500 versions/extras), 300 TV shows, 15000 episodes, ~1.1k seasons, 20000 actors, ~42k cast links; 3000 artists, 4000 albums, 40000 songs, ~53k song-artist and ~52k song-genre links; ~24k art rows
visibility_note: 21k stars; Kodi's library runs on SQLite by default on every platform (MySQL/MariaDB optional), on millions of TV boxes and HTPCs
interest_note: Library pages go through heavy views: movie_view (8 joins, correlated EXISTS, CASE filter), tvshow_view over two GROUP BY views, season_view grouping over tvshow_view, albumview with per-row correlated AVG/MAX; music filters stack nested correlated EXISTS; sort keys built from CASE/LIKE/SUBSTR.
reach_note: millions of installs across PCs, TV boxes and Raspberry Pi media players
